step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core system components from the visual diagram and audio transcript: Monolith Data (ThirdParty), Amazon S3, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS Secrets Manager, and AWS KMS.
2. Analyzed the flow of data decomposition from the legacy Monolith Data into specific AWS services: Binary data to S3, Relational data to Aurora, Key-Value pair configuration data to DynamoDB, and sensitive Encrypted data to Secrets Manager.
3. Identified the security and multi-tenant key management flow where AWS KMS provides per-tenant encryption keys across all target data stores (S3, Aurora, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager).
4. Formatted nodes and edges using valid vocabulary and strict schema rules.

graph.name: OutSystems Monolith Data Decomposition Architecture
graph.notes: OutSystems decomposes its legacy monolith database into purpose-built AWS storage and database services (S3, Aurora Serverless, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager) with multi-tenant encryption managed by KMS.

nodes.name: Monolith Data
nodes.notes: Legacy monolith data containing Binary, Relational, Key-Value, and Encrypted components.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores unstructured binary blob data and unstructured document files.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Aurora Serverless used for per-tenant core relational application definitions.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores configuration data and key-value pairs offloaded from relational storage.

nodes.name: Secrets Manager
nodes.notes: Securely stores sensitive encrypted data directly instead of pre-encrypting in relational DB.

nodes.name: KMS
nodes.notes: Generates per-tenant keys enabling multi-tenancy and Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) encryption strategies.

edges.notes: Offloads binary unstructured data to S3.
